Arranged in **ascending order**, the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for ${0}^{∘}<x\le {360}^{∘},$ are $x=${{field-1}}${}^{∘}$ and $x=$
{{field-2}}${}^{∘}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2})={30}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${30}^{∘}$ lies inside the required domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={30}^{∘}.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}={30}^{∘}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/d88379fcad6ee1bfc7f6c2159c814f92ca330dbacee191ebebb027bab306fe2c.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={360}^{∘}-{\theta }_{R} \\  & ={360}^{∘}-{30}^{∘} \\  & ={330}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the solutions of the equation, arranged in ascending order, are $x={30}^{∘}$ and $x={330}^{∘}.$
